headline: Virginia's Clean Slate Act Automatically Erases Eligible Records
meta_description: Starting October 1, Virginia automatically seals eligible criminal records without requiring applications, fees, or hearings—affecting roughly 415,000 people.
summary_short: Virginia's groundbreaking Clean Slate Act went fully into effect on October 1, automatically closing eligible records to public view—no paperwork required.
body:
Virginia's Clean Slate Act reached full effect on October 1, fundamentally changing how the state handles criminal records. Rather than requiring individuals to navigate applications, pay fees, or attend hearings, the state's own systems now automatically identify eligible records and seal them from public view.

This shift affects approximately 415,000 people whose records will be closed without any action on their part. The automation removes traditional barriers that often prevented people from accessing relief they qualified for—eliminating paperwork, cost, and the stress of legal proceedings.

The change represents a significant step toward giving people second chances. By making record sealing routine and invisible to the person affected, Virginia has transformed what was once a complicated legal process into a systematic clearing of the slate.
quick_facts: Virginia's Clean Slate Act took full effect October 1
Records automatically sealed with no application or fee required
Approximately 415,000 people affected by the change
State systems now automatically identify and close eligible records
